svg.title: Publish-time architecture of the related-articles pipeline
svg.desc: Posts are split into blocks; google/gemini-embedding-2 embeds blocks and openai/gpt-6-luna extracts facts and reranks candidates, both through OpenRouter at publish time; a graph ranker, a lexical ranker and an embedding ranker propose up to 15 candidates; one JSON record per post is committed to Git; the build checks the records without API keys and renders a static site.

g.text: Publish time: on the publishing machine, with API keys
this step calls that model through OpenRouter
API keys, vectors and model calls stay above this line
Site build and page view: no API key, no model, no vectors
The list and its graph are static HTML and SVG drawn at build time.
A page view calls no model and no API.
113 Markdown posts, cut into blocks: one paragraph, code block,
table row, caption or list item, at most 480 characters, with a
SHA-256 of its text; 3,826 blocks in use
pins first, then one from each ranker in turn; duplicates and
up to 3 blocks per side of each candidate pair: blocks linking to
the other post, fact evidence, then the nearest by embedding
1 call per post, all its candidates; 0–4 picks, each a relation
type, one Korean sentence, 2 block indices
a pick must name a candidate, a relation type allowed for the
pair and two existing blocks; code attaches quotes and hashes.
A rejected answer stores nothing for that post.
One JSON record per post, committed to Git
facts, candidates with block ids, picks with quoted blocks,
two input hashes, model id and settings
each record against the current text: both input hashes,
quoted blocks, relation types, excluded pairs
blocks not yet in the cache
